decisions.rationale: The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage under the Wouldn't It Be Nice track context. The passage directly states the frustration of youth, what one cannot have, what one wants, and waiting for it.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage in the You Still Believe In Me context. The passage supports Wilson closing his eyes, entering a world, singing more effeminately and sweetly, and allowing more love to come through him.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage under That's Not Me. The passage supports the Mike Love-ish characterization, the powerful souped-up vocal description, and Wilson and Tony Asher not realizing who they were writing for.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted Don't Talk passage. The passage directly supports that the song resulted from many ways to tell someone you love them and that Wilson and Asher had a special grip on that kind of thing.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage in the I'm Waiting for the Day context. The passage supports Wilson's view that his vocal sounded weird in his head, that it was the one album cut he did not like much, and that it was very positive.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage under Let's Go Away for Awhile. The passage supports Bacharach's influence, similar chord changes, and Wilson saying he was proud of the tune.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted Sloop John B passage. The passage directly supports Al Jardine asking for the song, the Kingston Trio version, Jardine bringing and playing the record, and Wilson learning and arranging it.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage under God Only Knows. The passage supports Wilson saying it was his and Tony Asher's vision and describing the blind/eyes-closed image of seeing a place or event.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage naming I Know There's An Answer. The passage supports that an organ and tack piano together create a completely new or different sound.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage under Here Today. The passage supports that Wilson called it a mystery song, did not really know what it was about, both liked and did not like it, and did not identify with it like other songs.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage under I Just Wasn't Made For These Times. The passage supports Wilson's behind-the-beat description and the idea of creating the song from a place.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage under Pet Sounds. The passage supports that the instrumental was originally Run James Run, was intended as a James Bond theme type of song, and was put on the album after they thought getting it to the James Bond people would not happen.

The claimId is unique and stable-looking. The referenced artifactId and URL match the fetched artifact, and the declared offsets exactly select the quoted passage under Caroline, No. The passage supports Wilson calling it probably his favorite cut and saying his father suggested speeding it up a whole note, which they did.
